source: Bush, R. 2008. 'Nutrition', ACIAR AH 2005/086 workshop slides, University of Sydney (mekonglivestock.wordpress.com)
text: Two basic forage-conservation methods are described. Hay: dry grass in the sun and protect it from rain -- this preserves nutrients for a long period. Silage: more labour-intensive, requiring a pit 1.5-2.0m deep; young grass is chopped into 4-6cm lengths (older grass into shorter 1-3cm lengths) and compacted into layers 30-40cm deep, then covered thoroughly with soil to exclude air from the finished pit, which is essential for proper preservation.
